MEMORANDUM ORDER: Accordingly, the Court finds that the New York Times and Daily News have not demonstrated good cause justifying their requests for leave to amend their complaints to add new theories of contributory copyright infringement liability against Microsoft. In sum, OpenAI's Rule 12(c) motion (Dkt. No. 1586) is denied as moot as to the News Plaintiffs because the News Plaintiffs have agreed to exactly what OpenAI sought in its motion: dismissal with prejudice of their "material contribution" contributory copyright infringement claims against OpenAI. The Court dismisses with prejudice the News Plaintiffs' "material contribution" contributory copyright infringement claims against OpenAI and Microsoft premised on alleged direct infringement by end users. The Court also dismisses with prejudice the trademark dilution claims by the New York Times and the Daily News. The New York…

MEMORANDUM ORDER: Accordingly, 1. OpenAI's motion for judgment on the pleadings pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 12 (c) dismissing Ziff Davis's contributory copyright infringement claim is denied as moot. 2. Ziff Davis's cross motion requesting leave to file a Second Amended Complaint dismissing its contributory copyright infringement, federal trademark dilution, and state-law trademark dilution claims is decided as follows: a. Ziff Davis's contributory copyright infringement claim that has been stayed and its federal and state-law trademark dilution claims that have been stayed-i.e., those claims that concern the models o1, o1 mini, o1-pro, GPT 4.1, GPT-4.5, o3, o3-mini, o4-mini, and GPT-5-are dismissed without prejudice. b. It is well established that a corporation cannot appear pro se, and must be represented by a lawyer. See Grace v. Bank Leumi Trust Co. of NY, 443 F.3d 180, 192 (2d Cir. 2006) ([I]t is settled law that a corporation may not appear in a lawsuit against it except through an attorney.); see also Age Reversal Unity v. New York Univ., 24-CV-4808 (MMG), 2024 WL 3521759, at *2 (S.D.N.Y. July 24, 2024). Accordingly, the proposed intervenor's motion is DENIED. coverage.headline: OpenAI Says NY Times Seeks Sanctions Due to Lack of Evidence
coverage.summary: OpenAI filed its opposition brief on August 14, telling Judge Stein that publishers have 'no evidence whatsoever' that ChatGPT systematically regurgitates their articles and that its claim of hiding search capabilities is an attempt 'to rewrite history.' OpenAI maintained it followed court orders to preserve ChatGPT conversations 'to the letter' and made 'herculean efforts' to produce training data and tens of millions of outputs.

coverage.headline: OpenAI Fights Sanctions Bid In News Copyright MDL
coverage.summary: OpenAI urged Judge Sidney Stein to reject sanctions that would bar it from relying on a 20 million-chat evidence sample, arguing it neither violated the preservation order nor misrepresented its ability to search for copyrighted material. The filing is the company's formal opposition to the 17-publisher coalition's sanctions motion in the consolidated MDL.

coverage.headline: OpenAI says news outlets' sanctions motion seeks to 'rewrite history'
coverage.summary: OpenAI pushed back on allegations from the NYT-led publisher coalition that it obstructed discovery in the MDL copyright case, calling the sanctions bid an 'end run around proving their case' and defending spending 'hundreds of hours and millions of dollars' on what it described as one of the most complex evidence productions in U.S. litigation history.

coverage.headline: New York Times and Other News Outlets Accuse OpenAI of Lying in Discovery, Demand Legal Sanctions Against AI Giant
coverage.summary: Variety reported on the sanctions motion, noting the Times has spent more than $28 million in total litigation costs against AI companies, with $4.2 million incurred in the first quarter of 2026 alone. The Daily News, Center for Investigative Reporting, and Ziff Davis are among the co-plaintiffs in the consolidated MDL.

coverage.headline: New York Times, publishers seek sanctions against OpenAI
coverage.summary: Quartz reported that publishers contend OpenAI rendered billions of ChatGPT exchanges inaccessible through deletion or by stripping them of searchability, and that OpenAI had already built an internal database of roughly 78 million de-identified ChatGPT conversations before the Times filed suit. Publishers sought monetary penalties, attorney fees, and an adverse evidentiary finding regarding their copyrighted works.

coverage.headline: Deposition Reveals OpenAI Tracked Its Own Copyright Violations While Claiming It Could Not
coverage.summary: The article details the 17-publisher coalition's allegation that OpenAI ran internal searches for copyright-infringing content while simultaneously telling the court such searches were technically impossible, and that it deleted billions of ChatGPT conversation logs ordered to be preserved. If the sanctions motion succeeds, it could hand publishers a trial-altering evidentiary win without requiring merits proof.

coverage.headline: OpenAI faces sanctions bid as copyright case escalates
coverage.summary: Publishers are asking Judge Stein to bar OpenAI from using its 20-million-log evidence sample and to rule as established fact that the logs would show ChatGPT reproduced their journalism — a remedy that Times lead attorney Ian Crosby said would resolve the case's most contested technical question without a trial.

coverage.headline: NYT-Led Publishers Escalate Copyright Fight, Seek Court Sanctions Against OpenAI
coverage.summary: The publishers' filing alleged that 'OpenAI misled the Court and News Plaintiffs regarding its existing technical capacity all while continuing to compress and delete billions of conversation logs,' while OpenAI denied the allegations, citing user privacy concerns.

coverage.headline: New York Times Seeks Sanctions Against OpenAI in Copyright Case
coverage.summary: Bloomberg Law reported on the publishers' motion accusing OpenAI of a 'deliberate and systemic effort to obstruct discovery,' alleging a two-year concealment of its ability to search ChatGPT training data and output logs for copyrighted works. The motion argues the deception prevented publishers from establishing the foundation of their copyright case.

coverage.headline: News Outlets Seek Sanctions on OpenAI in US Copyright Litigation
coverage.summary: MLex reported on the sanctions motion filed in the S.D.N.Y., quoting the publishers' filing that OpenAI's concealment 'withheld highly relevant evidence, prolonged discovery, inflated expenses, and burdened the court.' The motion directly challenges OpenAI's representations about its technical search capabilities.

coverage.headline: New York Times says OpenAI hid evidence in ChatGPT copyright trial
coverage.summary: Publishers allege OpenAI falsely claimed for years it lacked the ability to search its training corpus and ChatGPT output logs, and that it deleted billions of ChatGPT outputs in violation of the court's preservation order and substituted millions of logs in the requested 20-million-record sample. Plaintiffs are asking the court to bar OpenAI from relying on that sample at trial and to enter adverse-inference findings.

coverage.headline: NYT-led group asks court to sanction OpenAI in US copyright dispute
coverage.summary: The New York Times, Daily News, and other media outlets asked a federal judge to impose sanctions on OpenAI, with publisher counsel alleging OpenAI made misrepresentations for two years about its ability to search training datasets for copyrighted content.

coverage.headline: New York Times Seeks Sanctions Against OpenAI in Copyright Case
coverage.summary: Bloomberg Law reported that the NYT and co-plaintiff publishers filed a motion accusing OpenAI of a 'deliberate and systemic effort to obstruct discovery' in the MDL copyright proceeding. The motion centers on allegations that OpenAI concealed search capabilities and deleted billions of ChatGPT conversation logs under a court preservation order.

coverage.headline: News Orgs. Want OpenAI Sanctioned In Copyright MDL
coverage.summary: Law360 reported on the earlier, January 2026 iteration of the discovery fight, detailing allegations that OpenAI failed to properly maintain or produce ChatGPT output logs in the MDL. This reporting laid the groundwork for the broader July sanctions motion.
